requiredFindings.title: The new umask test mutates the process-wide umask inside the shared parallel libtest process; the platform suite fails in parallel cargo test
requiredFindings.detail: libc::umask(0o177) in exclusive_regular_refuses_... applies to the whole test process while libtest runs the other 157 platform tests on parallel threads; entries they create in that window lose the owner-search bit. Under the README's documented `cargo test --locked --offline --workspace --all-targets` (default parallelism) the platform lib suite failed in 100/100 runs with 483 PermissionDenied fixture panics across other modules. Removing only the six umask lines (T0) returns to the base rate: 8/100, all one pre-existing unrelated test. The request's filtered command and serial runs pass, which is why they did not show it. The assertion itself is the only owner test that pins the r3 RF-1 ordering (N1) and the directory mode set (N2).
requiredFindings.fix: Keep the assertion but run it where the umask is not shared: re-exec the test binary for a single child test (--exact ... --test-threads=1, marker env var) that sets 0177, creates, restores and asserts, with the parent asserting the child's success (reviewer T1: 7/100 parallel failures, all the pre-existing test; child assertion passed 100/100; rustfmt clean; still kills the r3 ordering). Or factor the post-openat steps so a test drives them on a directory it created as 0600, with no umask at all.

observations.summary: More pinning is possible without injection: direct empty_directory tests on F1-F3 fixtures (the link count otherwise hides the scan on APFS) and a direct fresh_owned_directory test on 0600/0400 fixtures. The error paths (N4, N8) need an injected fault, which the reviewer dylib shows is possible on macOS.
Link count 2 is a filesystem convention (APFS counts every entry, ext4/xfs subdirectories, btrfs reports 1: fail-closed). Linux not replayed.
Identity not proven (same-owner empty directory accepted in the window; acceptable). create_exclusive_directory's doc still does not mention the owner/link/empty refusal or the scan-after-mode order.
Cost convention: the fstat buffer is not counted in bytes (carried).
close(scan) lacks a SAFETY comment; one SAFETY comment covers two cfg-selected unsafe blocks in clear_errno/current_errno (Linux blocks undocumented); the test's umask calls lack SAFETY comments.

descriptor_filesystem::tests::native_filesystem_original_file_lock_and_all_path_components_stay_owned fails ~7/100 parallel runs on the base (ChangedDuringRead); out of scope. Earlier reviewer replays used RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 and could not see parallel-only effects; this review measures both modes.

Security test lacks directory existing-entry/symlink cases; single_component error text says 'file'; residual entry after refusal and retry AlreadyExists; public unaccounted create_exclusive_*; openat mode style nit; unused From impls and nested WorkFailure.

limits: This macOS development host (APFS) only; Linux not replayed.
readdir faults were injected by interposition in the reviewer's copy of the test binary, not produced by a real I/O failure.
The mkdirat/openat window was analysed, not raced (N5).
Parallel-failure rates are over 100 runs on one 18-CPU host, not exact probabilities; the candidate's 100/100 is not borderline.
Mutation measures test strength, not proof.
